# Data Management Activities

In addition to its regular responsibilities for validating, processing, maintaining and disseminating fisheries data, the Data Section prepared datasets and supporting information for IOTC scientific and technical meetings throughout 2026, including TCAC16, WPICMM09, WPSE03, WGFAD08, WPTT28 (data preparatory and assessment sessions), WPNT16, WPB24, WPEB22, TCAC17 and WPDCS22. Alongside this recurrent work, the Secretariat continued to improve reporting tools, data validation, databases and online information services.

## Data Reporting

The Secretariat updated the [guidelines for reporting fisheries statistics](https://data.iotc.org/reference/guidelines/stats/index.html) and developed [guidelines for Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) data](https://data.iotc.org/reference/guidelines/ros/index.html). Reporting forms are increasingly managed through a [dedicated GitHub repository](https://github.com/iotc-secretariat/iotc-data-forms), supported by revised [form descriptions](https://data.iotc.org/reference/form-descriptions/index.html), including an updated [Form 7PR](https://data.iotc.org/reference/form-descriptions/stats/Form-7PR.html). Proposed amendments to Form 1RC to implement Resolution 26/06 are described in [IOTC-2026-WPDCS22-05](https://iotc.org/documents/WPDCS/22/05). The [IOTC Reference Data Catalogue](https://data.iotc.org/reference/latest/index.html) was also further developed, including standardised descriptions and code lists.

## Data Validation

Online validation tools are available for statistical reporting Forms 1DI, 1RC, 3BU, 3CE and 4SF, with associated development resources maintained in the [IOTC form-management repository](https://github.com/iotc-secretariat/iotc-lib-base-form-management). Work continued on validators for Form 3DA and ROS reporting forms, including the use of the [_vrule_ R package](https://github.com/fdiwg/vrule) to implement standardised validation rules. The validators are being migrated to FAO cloud infrastructure through the [IOTC Shiny App Catalogue](https://iotc.review.fao.org/shiny/app_direct/data_validators/), while further tools are planned for Forms 2FC, 3AA, 5MB and 7PR.

Further progress was made in modernising the Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) data processing and validation framework, with support from a dedicated consultancy under SWIOP (see below). This included the development and publication on CRAN of the R package [form.model](https://cran.r-project.org/package=form.model), which provides a standardised framework for describing versioned reporting forms, their structure, constraints and reference data requirements. Complementary R-based tools and procedures were developed to automate the extraction and validation of ROS submissions, including an initial assessment of 171 historical Version 3 files. This work provides the foundation for extending validation to Version 4 forms, improving interoperability with national systems and developing standardised data-loading and validation workflows.

## Data Management and Dissemination

The Data Section continued the annual processing and quality review of fisheries datasets, including work on discard and ROS data (see [IOTC-2026-WPDCS22-10](https://iotc.org/documents/WPDCS/22/10)). Developments also included the migration of databases to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS environment, improvements to reproducible data-processing workflows, and publication and dissemination of datasets and associated documentation.

Persistent identifiers and records are being developed through the [IOTC Zenodo Community](https://zenodo.org/communities/iotc_ctoi/records), covering data-related Conservation and Management Measures, fisheries statistics and ROS reporting forms, and IOTC code lists. DOI-based publication of nominal catch and tagging datasets remains in progress.

## Tools and Online Services

In preparation for the new IOTC website, the Secretariat reviewed the organisation of data-related web content around six areas: **Reporting**, **Regional Observer Scheme**, **Datasets**, **Tools**, **Data Services and Repositories**, and **Publications**. Development of the Tools area and migration of online services are ongoing.

## Scientific Projects

Two externally funded projects -- the EU-funded project supporting the Scientific Committee's Programme of Work (**EC1350**) and the **Sustainable Western Indian Ocean Programme (SWIOP)** -- provide additional support for fisheries data management, biological sampling and scientific capacity development. Their activities include modernisation of information systems, improvements to coastal fisheries data collection and processing, harmonisation of biological sampling, and regional training. The principal data-related components are summarised in [Appendix VI](#projects).
